title: Falsely representing oneself as a consumer

jurisdiction.name: European Union (applies where consumers in the EU are reached)

instrument: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive 2005/29/EC, consolidated text of 27.09.2026
binding_note: A directive, applied through each Member State's national law. Annex I lists practices that are unfair in all circumstances, and the text says the same single list applies in all Member States. It covers business-to-consumer practices: the party must be a trader.

in_force.note: Original Annex I point, in the 2005 text and unchanged in the consolidated version of 27.09.2026.

sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (Cellar), consolidated text
sources.note: EUR-Lex answered scripted requests with an empty 202 challenge, so the same document was read from the Publications Office repository that serves EUR-Lex. Consolidated version 02005L0029-20260927, the latest listed in Cellar on the retrieval date (earlier: 20220528). The consolidated text states it has no legal effect; the Official Journal texts are authentic.

quotes.text: Falsely claiming or creating the impression that the trader is not acting for purposes relating to his trade, business, craft or profession, or falsely representing oneself as a consumer.

elements.label: Posts present the speaker as an ordinary consumer giving their own view
The speaker is in fact a trader, or acts in the name of or on behalf of one
elements.note: For unlabelled posts this would be shown by contracts or agency records, not by the page.

elements.label: The impression is false
elements.note: Falsity depends on element B and on how the impression was created.

does_not_prove: A post that reads like a fan and shares a template with paid posts is not proof that its author was paid. A match on visible elements is a comparison with a published definition. It is not a finding by a court or a consumer authority, and it says nothing about elements Daylight Commons cannot see.
